invariants: Public create/resume holds an exact unpublished preparation until setup and commit succeed.
Enter both registries before session/created, agent/created and agent/session-start, in that order.
Caller abort, owner unload and factory unload stop pending load/setup without awaiting an uncooperative provider; late preparations release once.
A failed or disposed transaction cannot remove a later generation under the same session ID.
identity: One exact SessionPreparation.session per transaction; caller seed and signal are forwarded. Publication rejects competing live IDs.
ownership: Registry reads retain caller Context through Cordis Service tracing. Caller fiber owns the transaction, factory owns pending wrapper settlement and live teardown; published scope exposes its agent.
ordering: prepare -> unpublished scope/setup -> setup commit -> enter session -> enter agent -> session/created -> agent/created -> agent/session-start -> driver. Disposal is memoized and unregisters exact instances.
errors: Setup/commit/pre-aborted signal rejects before publication. Publication exceptions unwind entered instances and effects. Canonical Remote/SDK consumers preserve transaction failure and never pre-publish their session.
cancellation: Race caller/fiber/factory signals with load/setup. Abandoned provider result is observed and released; Python observer Task cancellation uses the same cleanup without cancelling the provider operation.
adaptation: Python 3.8 Futures and AbortController implement JS Promise races; asynchronous Python commit callbacks remain supported. Nine source-derived paired observations and local edge probes certify this bounded public factory closure, not all 100 official assertions. Configured startup/reload and wider Session persistence/replay remain separate Profile/Session work.

rc1_review.scope: Current finite executable provider/consumer corpora, original-browser and extracted observations in the single full receipt. Historical alpha evidence remains historical; no inventory-wide parity, arbitrary ABI/history, paid-provider or Win7 certification.
